walkthroughs.body_html:
Producing Robust Programs — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Producing Robust Programs brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Producing Robust Programs.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: What does inheritance allow a subclass to do?
options: Replace the superclass entirely.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
Reuse and extend the attributes and methods of its superclass.
The computer crashes.

mcqs.q: What happens when 11111111 + 1 is computed in an 8-bit register?
options: Copy code from any unrelated class.
The computer crashes.
It just becomes 100000000 normally.
Overflow - the result requires 9 bits but only 8 are available.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.
Because TCP cannot handle video data.
The computer crashes.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Algorithm”?
options: A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
Table used to track the changing values of variables as an algorithm executes step by step.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
